name: Wenquxing (文曲星)
blurb: A Chinese pocket electronic dictionary that students also used for games and BASIC
title: What Is Wenquxing (文曲星)? China's Electronic Dictionary and Games
description: Wenquxing (文曲星) is a Chinese electronic dictionary brand launched in 1995 by Beijing's Jinyuanjian. Students used it for English, games and GVBASIC programming.
answer: Wenquxing is a brand of pocket electronic dictionaries made by the Beijing company Jinyuanjian (金远见), first sold in October 1995 and named after a star associated in Chinese tradition with literature and exams. It cut the price of an electronic dictionary from around 2,000 yuan to three or four hundred, passed 20 million units sold by 2003, and later models doubled as tiny handhelds with games and GVBASIC programming. Smartphones pushed electronic dictionaries into a niche, but the Wenquxing brand still sells study devices today.

body: Jinyuanjian was founded in Beijing in 1993 to develop the Wenquxing dictionary; in Taiwan the line was sold under another name. The first model, the CC100 of October 1995, looked like a small card-style calculator and offered little more than an English–Chinese dictionary, a clock and a calendar.

Its big change was price. According to a retrospective in Jiemian, Wenquxing brought electronic dictionaries down from about 2,000 yuan to three or four hundred, and before 2000 the 298-yuan PC-260 and the 428-yuan talking PC-500 were among the most fashionable gadgets a student could own. A few hundred yuan was still a lot for a family.

ul: Yingxiong Tan Shuo (英雄坛说), a text-based martial-arts RPG set in "Peace Town" and inspired by MUD online games, written in assembly by Jinyuanjian, with later Platinum and Golden editions.
Built-in puzzles such as Reversi, Sokoban and the sliding-block puzzle Huarong Dao.
Writing and running GVBASIC programs on the device itself, for many the first taste of programming.
Fan-made and ported games such as Tetris, Battle City-style tank games and Monopoly-style board games, passed between classmates.
Playing under the desk during class with the dictionary hidden behind a textbook.

body: The Jiemian retrospective puts the decline down to competition from better-resourced brands such as BBK, Jinyuanjian falling behind in colour learning devices and reading pens, and the arrival of mobile phones, smartphones and handhelds like the PSP.

The brand is still alive: Jinyuanjian's official site lists Wenquxing electronic dictionaries, translation devices, repeaters and learning tablets. The classic game-playing models are out of production and live on through second-hand units, emulators and fans.

faq.a: Beijing Jinyuanjian (金远见), founded in 1993; the first Wenquxing came out in 1995.
A text-based martial-arts role-playing game built into the CC800, PC1000 and later models from 2000, with Platinum and Golden editions.
Yes, the brand still sells electronic dictionaries and study devices, but not the old models with games.
